- entailed: true only if license_class follows from the holder's own words under the project's approved rule below; where that rule does not decide, only if it follows strictly from the rights statement's own words. A media item with no rights_statement may only be unknown or rights-restricted.
- adds_information: true if license_class or credit claims more than the statement says under that rule, for example public-domain from a statement the rule does not cover, or a licence taken from an uploader's tag.
- atomic: true only if the record describes one item.
- source_type_ok: true only if the statement comes from the item's holder, not from an uploader-asserted field (an Internet Archive licence field or an unconfirmed Wikimedia Commons template), and the item depicts or belongs to Albert Einstein, not a namesake.
- The title and alt_text are published with the item: adds_information is also true if either states anything (a date, name, place, event, award or description) that the holder's page does not show or say.
- Approved rights rule: The project's approved rights rule for Library of Congress and National Archives items (user decisions 2026-10-09). It applies only to a source whose registry standing is the Library of Congress (loc.gov) or the U.S. National Archives (archives.gov), and only to the holder's own rights field in that source's snapshot. Library of Congress: a rights advisory that begins "No known restrictions on publication" or "No known restrictions on images made by the U.S. Government" (alone or followed by further sentences) means license_class public-domain. LoC's full wording "No known restrictions on images made by the U.S. Government; images copied from other sources may be restricted" (its second clause is part of the phrase, not a caveat) means public-domain only when the same LoC record gives positive evidence of government creation (its part_of or a creator with the role creator is Historic American Buildings Survey, Historic American Landscapes Survey, Historic American Engineering Record, or a "United States. <agency>" heading), no item field marks an outside entry ("challenge", "competition", "contest", "prize", as in a "HALS Challenge Entry"), every named creator or contributor carries a government affiliation in its own heading (a federal survey or a "United States. <agency>" heading; a staff role such as photographer alone is not enough, and a name with no role, such as a family member or owner, blocks it), and nothing in the record's title, notes, description, credits or image titles and captions says the image is a copy ("photocopy", "photocopies", "photocopied", "copied from", "copy of", "copy photograph", "recopy", "recopied", "photograph of a photograph", "reproduction of"); otherwise never usable. "No known restrictions on work by staff photographers" means public-domain only when the same LoC record credits (a name heading in its creator or contributor fields; in its statement of responsibility, notes or the rights text only a credit such as "photograph by <name>", "Photographer: <name>" or "<name>, photographer", never a mention of the name) a U.S. News & World Report staff photographer: Warren K. Leffler, Thomas J. O'Halloran, Marion S. Trikosko, John Bledsoe, Chick Harrity; otherwise the item is never usable. "No known copyright restriction" means public-domain only when the same LoC record is in the New York World-Telegram & Sun collection and credits a World-Telegram staff photographer (a photographer named in its creator or contributor field, "photo by <name>", or record text such as "staff photograph", "World-Telegram photo", "World-Telegram & Sun photo"); otherwise never usable. A record that credits a wire service or agency (Associated Press, AP Photo, AP Wirephoto, Wirephoto, Acme, United Press, UPI, International News Photo, INP, Underwood, Harris & Ewing, Wide World, Keystone, Bain News, Pacific & Atlantic) is never a staff photograph. An approved wording followed by a caveat that asserts a restriction ("may be restricted", "restrictions apply", "restrictions may apply", "copyright restrictions", "permission required", "permission is required", "not in the public domain", "may be protected", "privacy and publicity rights") is never usable; a following sentence that supports free status (such as "No renewal in Copyright office (checked ...)") or only points to more information ("For more information, see ...") does not block it. National Archives: a use restriction status of "Unrestricted" (useRestriction.status, a record created by the federal government; never the access restriction) means license_class public-domain. Library of Congress "Publication may be restricted" or "Rights status not evaluated", and National Archives use restriction "Restricted", "Restricted - Possibly", "Restricted - Partly", "Restricted - Fully", "Undetermined", mean the item is never usable: license_class must be unknown or rights-restricted. Public domain under this rule needs the rights_statement to be the holder's exact wording from that field. The rule never applies to a Wikimedia Commons file page or tag, or to any other host; there, license_class follows strictly from the holder's own statement.

verdict: "supported" only if quote_in_snapshot, entailed, atomic and source_type_ok are all true, adds_information is false, and no source in live_by_source is "not_found". Report reachability in live_by_source, not in the verdict: whether an unreachable source is acceptable is decided by the deterministic gates, per source. "refuted" if a quote or statement is missing (in a snapshot or a live source), or the evidence contradicts or does not support the record. Otherwise "unclear".
rationale: at most two sentences naming the specific problem, or "no problem found".
registry_suggestion: null, unless a source not listed in the authority registry is published by an archive, museum, government body, university, foundation or prize body that could be listed; then one line naming the publisher, its domain and the type it could have (for example "fi.edu: The Franklin Institute, institutional"). It is advice for a person who maintains the registry: it never changes another field or the verdict.

Return only JSON of this shape, with exactly one entry for each item above and each item's id exactly as written:
{"verdicts": [{"id": "<item id>", "verdict": "supported|refuted|unclear", "quote_in_snapshot": true|false, "live_by_source": [{"source_id": "<source id>", "result": "found|not_found|unreachable", "url": "<url checked>"}], "entailed": true|false, "adds_information": true|false, "atomic": true|false, "source_type_ok": true|false, "rationale": "<text>", "registry_suggestion": "<text>"|null}]}
